purpose: Spironolactone is used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and fluid buildup (swelling) caused by liver or kidney problems. It is also used to treat a condition called hyperaldosteronism, where your body makes too much of a hormone called aldosterone. Some doctors also prescribe it for hormonal acne or conditions like polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in women.
how_it_works: Your body produces a hormone called aldosterone that tells your kidneys to hold onto sodium and water, which can raise your blood pressure. Spironolactone blocks this hormone, so your kidneys get rid of extra salt and water through your urine. Unlike most water pills, this medication helps your body keep potassium, which is important for your heart and muscles.
common_side_effects: You may notice more frequent urination, especially when you first start taking it. Some people experience dizziness, headache, stomach upset, nausea, or feeling tired. Men may sometimes notice breast tenderness or enlargement. Women may notice changes in their menstrual periods.
warnings: Because this medicine keeps potassium in your body, you should avoid eating large amounts of potassium-rich foods or taking potassium supplements unless your doctor says it is okay — too much potassium can be dangerous for your heart. Tell your doctor right away if you notice muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, especially ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or blood pressure medicines.
typical_dosing: The typical starting dose is 25 mg to 50 mg once daily, though your doctor may adjust this based on your condition. Some people take up to 100 mg or more per day for certain conditions. It is usually taken with food to help reduce stomach upset. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
